# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 12 (PNEUMA Dynamic)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 12
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Now, about the cross: Moses provides a type of it when Israel is being attacked by foreigners. To remind the people under attack that their sins had handed them over to death, the Spirit speaks directly to Moses' heart — prompting him to make a sign of the cross and of the one who was going to suffer on it. The message: unless they trust in him, war will prevail over them forever.
2. So Moses stacked one weapon on top of another in the middle of the battle. Standing higher than everyone, he stretched out his hands. While he held his hands stretched out, Israel prevailed. Whenever he let them drop, they started dying.
3. Why? So that they would understand: there is no way to be saved except through hope in him.
4. And another prophet says this as well: "All day long I stretched out my hands to a people who refused to obey — who kept pushing against my righteous way."
5. Once more Moses gives a type of Jesus: showing that he would suffer but also give life — even though they would think they had destroyed him. The sign was this: when Israel was dying from the serpents, the Lord set up a serpent on a pole and said: "Let everyone who has been bitten look at it, and they will be saved." Is there any salvation in a serpent? Absolutely not — and that is exactly the point.
6. He has glory even in the middle of these types. The Father says to the Son: "Let us make humankind in our image and likeness. Let them govern the animals of the earth, the birds of the sky, and the fish of the sea." And when the Lord looked at his beautiful creation he said: "Grow and multiply and fill the earth." He was saying all this to the Son.
7. And I will show you how the Lord speaks to us. He makes a second creation in these final days. The Lord says: "Watch — I am making the last things like the first." That is why the prophet declared the good news to those who had sunk in the sea, to those in the abyss, and to those lying in the chambers of Sheol.
8. And the scripture also says: "Out of the mountains of Israel a branch came up, and it grew and became great." The branch is David; the mountains of Israel are Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
9. And: "In the last days the mountain of the Lord will appear, and the house of God will be lifted above all the hills." That is the appearing of our Lord.
